thread:
IncidentBot: :rotating_light: PAGING: Significant spike in 5xx and gateway timeouts observed from the mid-atlantic edge (region: mid-atlantic-1). Error rate rose from ~0.2% to 6.8% in the last 3m. Paging @SRE Oncall and @Maya Patel for immediate triage. Automated plays: circuit-breaker tripped on gw-pool-4; traffic is partially degraded. See trends: https://grafana.redwood/alerts/1769990123

Maya Patel: on it. pulling traces now. first step — confirm if this is an upstream (origin) or local edge problem. looks like 502/504 on gateway -> backend connection resets.

Rajesh Kumar: confirming — app-gateway logs show a lot of `tcp RST` to backend pool 4. suspecting backend worker OOMs or kernel-level connection drops. No deploys in the last hour per DeployBot.

DeployBot: notice: no successful deploys to mid-atlantic services in last 60m. last deploy: release/1.24.2 @ 1769983200 by alexr.

Lucy Chen: I see elevated queue depth on the edge proxy (queue_len ~460, threshold 200). Autoscaler didn't kick for edge-pool-4. Might be healthcheck flapping causing slow scale.

Maya Patel: trying quick health check on backends:
```
$ curl -sv https://backend-midatlantic.internal/health || true
* TCP connection reset by peer
* Connection failed
```
This matches the RSTs.

Alex Romero: running `kubectl get pods -n mid-atlantic -l app=backend -o wide` — a few pods show `OOMKilled` in last 7m. Pod restart storms on node nax-03. Might be a memory regression or traffic spike.

Rajesh Kumar: rolling stacktrace grep for the OOMs; attaching a small sample log snippet:
```
OOMKilled: java.lang.OutOfMemoryError: Java heap space
at com.redwood.request.Handler.process(Handler.java:342)
```
Looks like a heap pressure regression in backend 2.

Maya Patel: immediate mitigations we should consider: 1) drain nax-03 and cordon, 2) scale backend pool to handle burst, 3) shift traffic away from mid-atlantic to nearby region (us-east-1) for user requests while we stabilize. Thoughts? :thinking_face:

SRE Oncall: agree with staged approach. Do not shift all traffic at once — use incremental failover policy: 10% -> 30% -> 60% over 5m steps. Keep canary for important SaaS customers. We'll also open incident page and notify CS.

Lucy Chen: starting cordon/drain on nax-03 now. Command:
```
kubectl cordon nax-03 && kubectl drain nax-03 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=60
```

CS Pager: tagging this as potential customer-impacting. Preparing a brief for top-20 customers and support SLA owners. ETA for first customer note: ~15m.

Alex Romero: increasing replica count for backend deployment (mid-atlantic):
```
kubectl scale deploy/backend --replicas=8 -n mid-atlantic
```
Scaling started; watch for new pods becoming ready.

IncidentBot: Autoscaling action suggested by Redwood Optimize: increase heap via configmap or route traffic to stronger instance types. Recommendation: quick fix is horizontal scale + failover; long-term patch required.

Maya Patel: while scaling completes, let's initiate gradual traffic shift. I'll create a temporary routing rule in the traffic manager to steer 10% to us-east-1. Command snippet:
```
POST /v1/routing/shift
payload: {\n  "from":"mid-atlantic-1","to":"us-east-1","percent":10,"duration":"5m"\n}
```

Rajesh Kumar: applying shift now. watch proxies for 5xx rate falling.

(2m later)
Maya Patel: after first 10% shift -> global 5xx dropped from 6.8% -> 4.9%. queue_len reduced to 320 on pool-4. continuing.

SRE Oncall: proceed to 30% in 5m. keep monitoring latency and p50/p95 for top customers.

Lucy Chen: drain finished on nax-03. I've removed pod with repeated OOM; new pods are scheduling on nax-05 and nax-07. Observability: new instances show healthy memory headroom so far.

Alex Romero: capturing heap dump from one of the restarted pods for postmortem diff. Uploading to secure bucket.

Maya Patel: shifting to 30% now. Also toggling circuit-breaker threshold for gw-pool-4 to a higher failure ceiling to avoid aggressive tripping while backend repairs complete. Patch:
```
service.gw-pool-4.circuit_breaker.failure_threshold = 0.7 -> 0.85
```

Rajesh Kumar: note: increasing circuit threshold reduces safety margin; we should watch for error amplification. We'll restore when stable.

(6m later)
Maya Patel: at 30% shift -> 5xx down to 2.1%. p95 latency improved ~220ms -> 180ms. Some customers on mid-atlantic still show degraded RPCs (non-critical).

CS Pager: drafting customer-facing message now. Will post to status page with 'partial regional degraded performance' and link to incident page.

IncidentBot: New incident page created: https://status.redwood/incident/1769990123. Severity: P2 (regional partial outage). Owner: Maya Patel.

Lucy Chen: monitoring: no further OOMs after new pods scheduled and heap config unchanged. Suggest we hold traffic shift at 30% for 10m to validate.

SRE Oncall: agreed. keep 30% for 10m. run heap tuning postmortem and then decide on permanent route.

Maya Patel: logging runbook actions for postmortem: probable root cause — memory regression in backend leading to node-level OOMs, causing connection resets and gateway-level 5xx. Mitigations applied: cordon+drain, horizontal scale, gradual cross-region failover, circuit-breaker threshold adjustment.

Rajesh Kumar: will open an internal Jira: BACKEND-REGRESSION-176999 for heap regression, include heap dumps, logs, and exact pod IDs.

Alex Romero: postmortem note — check scheduled cron job 'daily-compress' that runs on nax-03 at minute boundary; there was a simultaneous heavy job that aligns with traffic spike. Could be compounding factor.

Maya Patel: action items assigned:
- Rajesh: triage heap regression, root cause, PR to fix memory leak. (ETA 48h)
- Alex: verify cron jobs and ensure heavy batch jobs are isolated or throttled. (ETA 24h)
- Lucy: add autoscaler policy to prefer rapid scale on proxy queue length >200. (ETA 12h)
- SRE Oncall: runbook update to include incremental failover steps and circuit breaker guidance. (ETA 72h)

(30m since start)
Maya Patel: holding steady. 5xx now at 0.6% regionally. beginning rollback of temporary cb threshold to previous value.

IncidentBot: All mitigation actions complete. Marking incident as mitigated. Will keep channel open for 2h monitoring and postmortem collection. :white_check_mark:

CS Pager: posting to status: "Service degraded for parts of Mid-Atlantic region between 17:12–17:42 UTC. Root cause: backend memory regression triggered node OOMs leading to connection resets; mitigations included scale up, node drain, and cross-region routing. We will follow up with postmortem and remediation plan."

Rajesh Kumar: uploading initial artefacts to the incident ticket.

Lucy Chen: leaving a short note in the ops-runbook about prioritizing queue_len metric for proxy autoscaling.

Maya Patel: thanks team. I'll own the postmortem writeup. Closing for now, stay on-call for 2h in case of recurrence. :heart:
